mentl/ca33132:
The crown-tier leak's mechanism is whole. `row_subsumes` reaches an open
body tail and returns true, and its own comment states both the reason
and the compensation: a still-open tail is "GENUINELY free ... vacuous at
the gate (the rebind at the gate closes it to the declared row)", and
rejecting such tails was measured at 646 false effect-mismatches on the
self-compile. The rebind does not happen, and the vacuity assumption
holds only for a monomorphic body — for a polymorphic HOF the tail is a
parameter's row a caller instantiates with real effects.

That makes the fix a bind at the declared-row gate, never a rejection and
never an edit to row_subsumes, which is a read by design. It also makes
this a dedicated arc rather than loop residue: crown-tier, every
annotated fn with an open tail in blast radius, with a known way to get
it wrong.

Consolidate the peer entry, which had grown by accretion to 175 lines
carrying six dead framings above the live one. It is 89 lines now with
the kills counted in one paragraph, per the census-to-zero law the docs
run on themselves. Record the arc in PLAN's standing cursor ahead of the
existing queue.

Docs only; boot and wheel source untouched. verify green, doc-truth
green.
mentl/cabfe15:
The banked probe asked whether the emit's singleton-install proof is per
call site. It is neither per-site nor per-handler: there is no emit-time
proof at all. singleton_perform_block emits, for every stateful
singleton op call site, LWorldResolve into a local and then an LIf whose
null arm is LInvariantFailure(SingletonUninstalled). The unreachable is
a runtime else-branch.

So a floor count is simply the number of stateful singleton call sites
in a build — 50 baseline, 52 in the variant because the variant adds
two — and it says nothing about what is installed. Two iterations of
design rested on that count. Both were wrong, and reading the emit's own
construction cost one grep.

The full backtrace, read whole rather than grepped, corrects the other
half. The trap is in lambda_329309 under op_map_collector_yield,
iterate_from, map$spr_initnNode_nLowExpr — inside the map's lambda,
which is lower_expr(field.init). Had ls_enter_frame floored it would sit
directly under lower_state_field_inits. It does not: the frame call
succeeds. And the context is the demand walk — lower_pipe,
project_nested_fn, lower_stmt_body, reach_construct_loop,
reachable_from_main.

So the special case is a shortcut around lower_expr's VarRef path, not
around a missing frame. The bare config ref works because it never
enters that path; the nested case fails because it must. The fix that
follows is to resolve config refs structurally at every depth without
entering the general VarRef lowering. The frame was never the mechanism,
and lower_state_init was right to resolve by name all along.

Unmeasured and named rather than assumed: which op inside the VarRef arm
floors in this walk. The design does not depend on it.

mentl/ca40e08:
`type X = Y where pred` IS a refinement-type-alias, NOT a sum type with
variant Y. The seed's $parse_variants greedily consumed Y as a variant
in BOTH cases. For the refinement form, this re-registered Y in env's
ConstructorScheme, overwriting Y's original tag_id with X's variant
position (0). Every site constructing Y (e.g., `Span(sl, sc, el, ec)`)
got the wrong tag — variant-construction returned a nullary sentinel
rather than a heap variant. Downstream patterns destructuring Y read
garbage, dereferenced "Span" string bytes as pointer (0x6e617053 trap).

Detection: when $parse_variants returns, parse_type_decl checks for
TWhere at the next position. If present, $skip_predicate_to_stmt_end
absorbs the predicate (Lock #6 pragmatic skip, named follow-up
Hβ.first-light.refine-predicate-parser still owns full predicate
parsing); ADDITIONALLY now overwrites $variants_r with an empty list
so TypeDefStmt(name, [], []) carries no variants. Refinement alias
registers X as a type name without polluting Y's constructor binding.

Composes with: a8cf28e (PVar/PEVar disambiguation — same class of
bug, different mechanism — both were name-collision in ConstructorScheme
env entries).

Next gate (not closed by this commit): mentl2 on `type ValidSpan =
Span where ...`-bearing input still traps mid-parse via a separate
path — parser_compound/binop/primary chain hits a diagnostics_handler
that fault-reads "Span" string. Pattern-vs-expression dispatch in
the wheel's parser appears load-bearing on the same input; deeper
investigation needed.
